item.title: Pâtes à la crème de courgettes
item.description:
• Temps de préparation : 30 min
  • Difficulté : facile ★

Ingrédients

Pour 4 personnes

  • Courgettes : 800 g
  • Ail : 3 gousses
  • Parmesan : 100 g
  • Pâtes : 400 g
  • Pignons de pin
  • Herbes de Provence
  • Poivre et sel
  • Huile d’olive

Préparation

  1. Lavez les courgettes et râpez-les.
  2. Émincez la gousse d’ail et faites-la revenir dans une poêle avec un peu d’huile d’olive pendant quelques minutes.
  3. Ajoutez les courgettes râpées à la poêle et faites-les revenir pendant 6-7 minutes, jusqu’à ce qu’elles soient tendres.
  4. Une fois les courgettes cuites, versez les 3/4 dans un blender. Ajoutez le parmesan, les herbes de Provence, le sel et le poivre. Mixez jusqu’à obtenir une crème bien lisse.
  5. Faites cuire des pâtes selon les instructions du paquet. Une fois cuites, égouttez-les et mélangez-les à la crème de courgettes. Incorporez le reste des courgettes râpées pour ajouter de la texture.
  6. Servez les pâtes dans des assiettes, ajoutez quelques pignons de pin préalablement grillés et du parmesan râpé par-dessus.

Références

  • Recette d’origine : Pâtes à la crème de courgettes

item.title: Using Nox with PDM
item.description:
Nox and PDM are both fantastic Python development tools. However, their opposite stances towards virtual environment usage makes using them together a little more cumbersome. In this note, I’ll explain how I integrated Nox in my PDM workflow.

We will use Nox to automate testing on multiple Python versions during CI. We’d also like to run our tests using a similar command locally without having to maintain almost duplicate Nox sessions. We’ll therefore try and vary the Nox session’s behaviour using Nox and PDM features.

item.title: Conda Workflow
item.description:
This page describes my Conda workflow.

Conda

I use Conda as my environment and package manager. This choice is the outcome of a long professional history. Pros for choosing Conda:

  • it’s portable;
  • it’s simple to use;
  • it provides optimised binaries for several scientific packages;
  • it saves space on my hard drive;
  • it can install more than just Python stuff.

Cons:

  • many packages are missing (and interoperability with Pip has many issues when one starts playing with dependency pinning);
  • usually second-class citizen in CI workflows (see also previous point about deps pinning);
  • Conda’s dependency resolution is slow;
  • many people don’t use Conda.

My Conda workflow is consequently an attempt at overcoming some of these issues.

item.title: About
item.description:
About

The Human Who Wrote This

I’m Vincent, a research software engineer working for Brussels-based company Rayference. I have a PhD in thermal sciences and I work now on radiative transfer modelling and simulation applied to Earth observation.

I believe in the virtues of sharing: we achieve greater things through cooperation than competition, where greater is to be understood from the angle of wisdom rather than cleverness. My desire to contribute to open-source is a manifestation of this.
